title: Standard electrode potentials, cross-check table

source.name: Wikipedia, 'Standard electrode potential (data page)' (secondary compilation; its rows cite the CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics 87th ed. and other sources per row)
source.retrievedVia: raw wikitext (action=raw), values transcribed programmatically then read by hand
source.conditions: V vs SHE; 298.15 K; unit activity for aqueous species, solvent and pure solids/liquids; gases at 101.325 kPa (the table notes this is the common literature convention, not the current 100 kPa standard state)

toleranceNote: Different compilations of the same couple differ by several mV (rounding to 2 decimals in the table, older vs newer evaluations). 0.025 V is wide enough to accept those differences and narrow enough to catch a wrong sign, a wrong couple or a misplaced digit. It is not a claim that every PocketChem value is accurate to 0.025 V.

knownSpread.Au: The table lists 1.52 V; PocketChem uses 1.498 V (a value of the CRC kind). The 0.022 V spread is real source variation, not a transcription error, and is inside the tolerance.
knownSpread.Cu: The table lists 0.337 V; PocketChem uses 0.342 V (the value of the later CRC evaluation). 5 mV spread.
knownSpread.Fe: The table lists -0.44 V (rounded); PocketChem uses -0.447 V. 7 mV spread.
knownSpread.Sn: The table lists -0.13 V (rounded); PocketChem uses -0.138 V. 8 mV spread.
